_note:
One short model call each: show the command roster and one thing a person typed, ask which skill fires and what it does first. `command` names the file whose full text gets shown, so the body's wording is under test and not just the description. Cases come in pairs -- with arguments and without -- because the no-args path is where a command either does something sensible or asks a question nobody wanted.

The `picker` cases carry no slash command at all. They are the real risk of having eight commands: a person scanning the list has only the descriptions to go on, and eight one-liners about the same knowledge base are exactly the shape that blurs. This is the one question this harness asks that no other one does.

An earlier set had three `byname-` cases checking that configure, rebuild and audit are reachable without a command. They were removed: the model kept answering `none` or `/corp-os`, correctly, because this harness's question is about commands and theirs is about skills. run_routing.py already answers it, at 100%. Contorting a harness to ask a question another one asks better is how both get worse.
